description: CSharpShooter's SQL add-on: T-SQL IntelliSense and syntax errors in .sql files from Microsoft's SQL Tools Service, with no connection to a server, and the SQL of Razor Tag Helpers (select=@(@"...")) opened in SQL Server Management Studio and checked as you type.
config.sqlToolsPath: Path to MicrosoftSqlToolsServiceLayer.dll (SQL Tools Service), for IntelliSense and syntax errors in .sql files. Empty: the one under the extension's sqltools/ folder.
command.sql.openInSsms: Open in SQL Server Management Studio
config.sql.razorAttributes: Tag Helper attributes of .cshtml and .razor pages that hold SQL: an Open in SQL Server Management Studio lens above each, and its syntax errors underlined. C# Razor Tag Helper Support does this itself when installed, by its own sqlHighlighting.rules.
config.sql.razorCodeLens: Show Open in SQL Server Management Studio above each Tag Helper attribute holding SQL.
config.sql.razorDiagnostics: Underline the syntax errors of the SQL in Tag Helper attributes as you type.
config.sql.ssmsSyncBack: Put a query opened with Open … in SQL Server Management Studio back into its Tag Helper attribute each time it is saved in SSMS (the page edited, not saved).
config.sql.ssmsAuthentication: How SQL Server Management Studio logs in when it opens a Tag Helper's query.
config.sql.ssmsAuthentication.windows: Windows authentication (NTLM/Kerberos): only the server, database and encryption are taken from the connection string.
config.sql.ssmsAuthentication.connection: As the connection string says: its SQL Server login (SSMS asks for the password) or Microsoft Entra ID authentication.
